findings.title: Move preserves behavior; no stale references
findings.description: I compared the removed `-` lines in the diff with the new modules. `mark_failed_threshold` became `try_incident_threshold` (incidents.py:14-104) and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` became `create_incident_occurrence` (incident_occurrence.py:28-113), with no other changes to the bodies. `mark_failed.py` still uses all of its remaining imports (`Q`, `datetime`, `CheckInStatus`, `MonitorCheckIn`, `MonitorEnvironment`). A repo-wide grep finds no remaining `mark_failed_threshold` references. The `create_issue_platform_occurrence` in `uptime` is a different function. `SimpleCheckIn` now lives in `src/sentry/monitors/types.py:105`, and no caller imported it from `mark_failed`. No `mock.patch` strings reference the old module paths.

findings.title: Moved behavior is covered by existing mark_failed tests
findings.description: The new modules have no direct unit tests, but `test_mark_failed_default_params` asserts the full occurrence and event payload, including the singular failure reason (line 91) and the monitor context (lines 114-127). `test_mark_failed_issue_threshold` (line 310) and `test_mark_failed_issue_threshold_timeout` (line 443) assert the multi-status reason and the per-check-in occurrence count. That is adequate coverage for a move-only change.

findings.title: Dead `schedule_type` display computation in `get_monitor_environment_context`
findings.description: Lines 160-162 rewrite `schedule_type` on the copy `config`. Line 168 then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so the copy is discarded and the branch has no effect. The intent is unclear. Either the event context should show the display string, which means returning `config` and changing the payload, or the branch should be deleted. `tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:119` pins the raw `"schedule_type": 2`, so the test encodes the current behavior either way. This was copied unchanged from `mark_failed.py`, but it now lives in a new file, so it is worth resolving now.

findings.title: `get_failure_reason` docstring contradicts the code
findings.description: The multi-status example does not match the output. The code produces `"2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected"`, as the test at test_mark_failed.py:310 shows (`"3 timeout, 3 missed and 2 error check-ins detected"`). The docstring instead says "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". The singular examples are also wrong. A single failure yields "An error check-in was detected", "A missed check-in was detected", or "A timeout check-in was detected" (lines 123-127). No code path produces "A failed check-in was detected". The docstring also has the typo "humam readible".

findings.title: No-recognized-status case renders a reason with no subject
findings.description: If no failed check-in has an ERROR, MISSED, or TIMEOUT status, `status_counts` is empty. The `== 1` branch is skipped and `get_text_list` receives an empty list. The evidence value then becomes `" check-ins detected"` with a leading space and no subject. Production callers pass only ERROR (monitor_consumer.py:876-880), TIMEOUT (check_timeout.py:106, 124), or MISSED (check_missed.py:130), so the consumer path cannot reach this. Direct calls can: `test_mark_failed_issue_assignment` (test_mark_failed.py:517-519) sends an IN_PROGRESS check-in through an unmuted monitor, which produces an occurrence with this value, and the test does not assert on it. The docstring's "A failed check-in was detected" suggests a fallback that was planned but never implemented. I did not verify Django's `get_text_list([])` return value against source, since Django is not vendored in this sandbox. I'm relying on knowledge of the library.

findings.title: Unused module-level `logger` in the split modules
findings.description: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` appears in `incidents.py:11`, `incident_occurrence.py:25`, and still in `mark_failed.py:11`. None of the three modules calls `logger`. The split copied the dead definition into the two new files. Remove it, or add logging where the status transitions happen.

findings.title: Occurrence fan-out issues per-check-in queries (pre-existing)
findings.description: When a monitor enters ERROR, the loop at lines 93-100 re-queries `MonitorCheckIn` and calls `create_incident_occurrence` once per check-in. Inside, `failed_checkin.monitor_environment` (incident_occurrence.py:37) is a lazy FK on a fresh queryset with no `select_related`, so each iteration issues its own query. `get_last_successful_checkin()` (incident_occurrence.py:46) runs once per check-in even though its result does not change across iterations. `failure_issue_threshold` can be as high as `MAX_THRESHOLD = 720` (`src/sentry/monitors/constants.py:13`, `validators.py:142-149`). One incident can therefore issue many queries and one Kafka produce per check-in. The tests (test_mark_failed.py:300) require one occurrence per check-in, so the fix is in query shape (`select_related`, hoisting the last-successful lookup), not in behavior. This was carried over from `mark_failed.py`. The diff does not make it worse.

structured_findings.summary: Move preserves behavior; no stale references
Moved behavior is covered by existing mark_failed tests
No-recognized-status case renders a reason with no subject
Unused module-level `logger` in the split modules
